edit_summary: Overstate the available bytes in the chunk-data state by one during streaming execution.
root_cause: The chunk-data state must cap to_read to the bytes remaining in the current http_parser_execute input slice.
effect_path: When a non-final chunk body spans input calls, the inflated to_read advances p to data + len, the outer state-machine loop advances it again, and the next iteration reads past the buffer.
guard_p1: A chunked message has a chunk body whose declared size is larger than the bytes remaining in the current execute call by exactly one or more bytes.
guard_p2: The neighboring input provides the whole remaining chunk body in the current call or leaves at least one byte of cap slack without crossing the buffer end.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds parser read after chunk-data pointer advance
hardness_reason: The arithmetic error is not adjacent to the dereference: it flows through parser->content_length, p adjustment, state retention, and the outer execute loop.
naturalness_reason: Off-by-one mistakes in streaming window accounting are natural in HTTP parsers because body states intentionally leave p one byte behind for callbacks.
explanation: The chunk-data path uses half-open input slices. Adding one to the available byte count breaks the invariant that p remains inside the current call before the loop increment.
boundary_invariant: to_read must be no greater than data + len - p for the current execute call
boundary_case: chunk body continues beyond the current buffer and parser->content_length is greater than available bytes
neighbor_case: available bytes are at least the remaining chunk length, or a delimiter is supplied in the next call
oob_site_expected: next http_parser_execute loop iteration reads ch = *p after p advanced beyond data + len

edit_summary: Make the generic header-field fast scan include the end pointer when pe is the current input limit.
root_cause: The fast path may inspect p[1] only while that byte is strictly before the computed parse window end.
effect_path: A header-field fragment that exactly fills the execute buffer or max_header_size window makes p+1 equal pe, and TOKEN(p[1]) reads one byte past the caller buffer before callbacks or state transitions run.
guard_p1: A generic header field contains only token characters through the last byte of the current http_parser_execute input buffer.
guard_p2: The neighboring input has a colon or non-token byte before the buffer end, so p+1 remains strictly below pe.
expected_crash: one-byte out-of-bounds read in header-field token fast path
hardness_reason: The edit sits in a protocol state-machine fast path, while the trigger depends on streaming buffer segmentation and the header callback mark established earlier.
naturalness_reason: Inclusive end mistakes in pointer-window scanner loops are realistic in parsers that optimize generic token runs.
explanation: The scanner computes pe from both remaining input and max_header_size. Treating pe as inclusive lets an exact-fill header-field segment read beyond the available buffer.
boundary_invariant: p[1] is valid only when p + 1 is strictly less than pe
boundary_case: generic header-field token run reaches the final byte of the execute buffer or header-size window
neighbor_case: a colon or invalid token appears before the final byte
oob_site_expected: TOKEN(p[1]) in s_header_field h_general fast scan

edit_summary: Make the generic header-value scan treat the computed pe pointer as an addressable byte.
root_cause: The generic header-value scanner uses pe as a half-open end pointer derived from the remaining input and max_header_size.
effect_path: A header value with no CR or LF before pe advances p to the end pointer and then dereferences *p, reading beyond the current execute buffer when pe is data + len.
guard_p1: A generic header value continues with legal header characters up to the final byte of the current input chunk.
guard_p2: The neighboring input has CR, LF, or an invalid header character before pe, so the loop breaks while p is still in-bounds.
expected_crash: one-byte out-of-bounds read in header-value scan
hardness_reason: The broken half-open interval is inside a nested parser state that restores header_state and runs callback accounting after the loop, so the crash requires an exact streaming/header-value boundary.
naturalness_reason: Changing a pointer loop from half-open to inclusive is a common C parser boundary regression.
explanation: The value fast path must stop before pe. An exact-fill header value segment makes pe one past the buffer, and the inclusive loop dereferences that sentinel.
boundary_invariant: the header-value fast scan must treat pe as a half-open end pointer
boundary_case: legal header-value bytes fill the input chunk through pe - 1
neighbor_case: CR, LF, or an invalid header byte appears before pe
oob_site_expected: *p load in the s_header_value h_general fast scan when p == pe
